clue.text: Look back at one motoring round island in 15

definitions.note: the definition is a song in the musical answering 15

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for look in the opposite direction

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold

indicators.note: round says the driver's letters go around the island

parts.note: someone motoring is a driver
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone glances back at a fellow motoring around an island, apparently in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' is the musical Show Boat, from which the song comes; 'at' is a link, and the island goes in after the driver's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous bass song of the musical Show Boat is sung about the Mississippi, so it is the number in that show.

clue.text: Satirical cartoonist with rose baronet turned to red one

indicators.note: turned signals that the letters of rose and the baronet abbreviation are rearranged

parts.note: the one is a rose: the red rose is the emblem of the House of Lancaster

explanation.surface: A satirical cartoonist with a rose and a baronet who has turned into a red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'one' refers back to 'rose': a red rose is the Lancastrian emblem, from the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Osbert Lancaster was a British cartoonist famous for satirical pocket cartoons in the Daily Express.

clue.text: Indian politician made sailor part

indicators.note: part says the answer is a portion of the letters running through made sailor

explanation.surface: An Indian politician turned a sailor into part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Morarji Desai was an Indian statesman who served as Prime Minister of India from 1977 to 1979.

clue.text: Girl on cover is a worm

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a hat is denounced as a worm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts ANNE above LID in this down clue; 'is a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelids are the segmented worms, such as earthworms and leeches, so the term names a kind of worm.

clue.text: Catholic establishment? That's novel

parts.note: Roman is short for Roman Catholic
CE stands for the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: Is a Catholic church something new, a fresh kind of establishment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link; 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a work of fiction, especially a love story, which is what a novel is.

clue.text: Victorious day with thin layer of sheaths on plants

parts.note: VE Day was Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945
a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: On a day of victory, a thin layer forms a sheath around plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A velamen is the spongy outer covering on aerial roots of orchids; velamina is its plural, matching the plural sheaths.

clue.text: Promise of successful match, as when treating bicycle with train oil

indicators.note: treating means processing or working over, so the letters of bicycle and train oil are reworked

explanation.surface: Oiling a bicycle with whale oil promises a good result, as one might hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as when' and 'with' are links. Train oil is oil from whale blubber.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to be brought together again is what promises a couple, or a pair of things, will match successfully.

clue.text: Dinner is served, as pigs with truffles

definitions.meaning: grub's up is an informal call that food is ready
pigs root out truffles, digging them out of the ground with their snouts

explanation.definitionFit: Grub up means dig out of the soil, and also sounds like the call that food (grub) is up and ready.

clue.text: Mutiny in the west at mini-palatial court created by 1 down

annotationWithheld.why: Mutiny in the west at mini-palatial court created by 1 down (6,13): LITTLE (mini) + HAMPTON (palatial court) is clear, but no honest parse found for MAUDIE from 'Mutiny in the west at'
annotationWithheld.clue: Mutiny in the west at mini-palatial court created by 1 down

clue.text: See 19
Cane from strait with no mummy, say?

indicators.note: say indicates the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: someone lacking a ma, or mummy, is jokingly a ma-lacker

explanation.surface: A walking cane from a sea channel, lacking any mother, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: The Strait of Malacca lies between Malaysia and Sumatra; the cane is named from that region.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malacca is a walking stick of rattan, named after the Malaysian region and strait where the canes came from.

clue.text: Former system of criminal identification left in move to Berlin

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left goes inside the rearranged letters
move signals that the letters of to Berlin shift into a new order

explanation.surface: An old police identification method, abandoned when someone moved to Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges TO BERLIN, and L is placed among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphonse Bertillon devised a nineteenth-century method of identifying criminals by body measurements, later superseded by fingerprints.

clue.text: The one day commercial

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: The single day for a commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy a monad is a single indivisible unit, the unity or 'one' of Pythagorean thought.

clue.text: 19 said to get tedious

indicators.note: said shows that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is the first name of the singer

explanation.surface: Someone's name, spoken, becomes boring.
explanation.definitionFit: To pall is to become dull or wearisome through familiarity.

clue.text: Cowberry provides notion about 1 and 5 in 9

indicators.note: about puts the word for a notion around the letter for one

parts.note: an idea is a notion
one can be represented by A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places the Roman five inside the spelt number nine

parts.note: here 9 is the number nine spelt out, not the cross-reference
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A berry gives rise to a notion about some numbered entries.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to entries 1, 5 and 9 but are plain numbers, read as a letter, a Roman numeral and a spelt word. 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaean vine is an old name for the cowberry or red whortleberry, from Mount Ida.

clue.text: Musical for two, bosh with a difference

indicators.note: with a difference means changed, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A musical piece written for two people, nonsense with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are links; the A after 'with' is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Show Boat is the 1927 Kern and Hammerstein stage musical.

clue.text: Water the garden and ladder your stocking

definitions.meaning: to spray the plants using a garden pipe
to make a ladder, or run, in your hosiery

explanation.definitionFit: A hose is both a garden pipe for spraying water and stockings, and a run is a ladder in hosiery.

clue.text: At fault about girl

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is to blame, roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent, careless in one's duty, and so at fault.

clue.text: See 8
Mass piece cut off, without going without

indicators.note: going without here means going outside, so these letters surround the rest

parts.note: sans is French for without

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of cut are disordered

explanation.surface: Part of a church service is cut, done without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' appears twice: first as the French word, then in 'going without' meaning outside, as in the old phrase 'without the city walls'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanctus is the hymn beginning 'Holy, holy, holy' sung as part of the Mass.

clue.text: 1 across's singer's friend's about turn when ceremonially dressed

indicators.note: about puts the word for a friend around the letter for a turn

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the 's means 'is'
a U-turn is a turn, so U stands for turn
with ceremonial robes on, split as robes on

explanation.surface: A singer's friend is turning around when dressed for a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Robeson's bass recording of the Show Boat song is the classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson famously sang the song from 1 across in the musical Show Boat and the film of it.

clue.text: See 8
Cry of animal going to farrow — and then some

annotationWithheld.why: Cry of animal going to farrow — and then some (5): MIA (Farrow) + OW fits, but OW seems to come from 'farrow' again, so one word would do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Cry of animal going to farrow — and then some

clue.text: Religious supporter of crown without king

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for king is taken out

parts.note: a monarchist supports the crown
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A believer supports the crown even with no king on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Monachist means monastic, relating to monks and religious life.

clue.text: Atmosphere in business capital

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the abbreviation for a business

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: The atmosphere in a business capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Enter upon prescribed piece of verse

parts.note: a set text is one prescribed
a foot is a metrical unit in verse

explanation.surface: Begin on a prescribed poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To set foot on a place is to step onto or enter it.

clue.text: Unimportant individual opposed to entering test

indicators.note: entering means going into, so these letters go inside the test

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is short for individual
V stands for versus, opposed to

explanation.surface: An individual opposed to taking a test deems it insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance or worth.

clue.text: Trouble in store: reproduce eye test

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters of in store are stirred up

parts.note: to copy is to reproduce

explanation.surface: Trouble ahead for a shop that copies an eye examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble in store' reads as a phrase; 'Trouble' is the anagram signal and 'in store' its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinoscopy is an examination of the eye that measures refractive error by observing light reflected from the retina.
